override.note: PARSER BASELINE (HYPOTHESIS — NOT a validated model). Every ⛑ below is an UNMEASURED estimate; hand-tune + record against a real fight before trusting any number. Mary is an SG/Water/Supporter/Burst I pure-sustain kit: every one of her five kit lines is a heal, a healing-amplifier, or a DEF buff — she carries ZERO damage effects and ZERO offensive stat buffs. Her sim-relevant surface is therefore TANDEM ONLY (HARD RULE: never skip heal/shield/DEF/HP lines on isolation): S1 emits a recovery event on every last bullet (per-magazine cadence), and the burst emits a team-wide recovery event on cast — both drive a teammate's 'recovery' trigger (e.g. crown's on-recovery consumer). Solo she moves no damage beyond her own SG normals. Trigger fidelity: S1 'when the last bullet hits' = lastBullet; S2 'when entering Full Burst' = fullBurstEnter (fires on ANY team Full Burst, not just rotations she bursts); the burst block is burstCast, and as a Burst I unit she casts on essentially every rotation. The burst's two ■ headers are authored as SEPARATE blocks because the second carries an activation clause the first does not. Heal AMOUNTS are deliberately unmodeled — the engine tracks no HP pool at scope lock — so the percentages live verbatim in unmodeled; the recovery EVENT is the modeled mechanic.

flags.estimate: ammo 9, reloadFrames 111, 1 pull per trigger — so ~1 recovery event per magazine, roughly every (9 shots ÷ SG pulls-per-sec) + 1.85s reload.
flags.reasoning: ALWAYS-⛑ #1: the cadence tuple is datamined and known-unreliable (rate_of_fire nominal vs 60fps-frame-boundary effective; reloadFrames likewise). Mary carries no ammo/reload modifiers of her own, so the tuple is the SOLE driver of how often her S1 recovery fires — and any teammate with an on-recovery damage consumer inherits that error one-for-one. This is her single highest-leverage unknown despite her having no damage of her own.
flags.recipe: Focus-record mary in a comp with an on-recovery carrier; count her reload cycles over a fixed 60s window from the ammo counter (the instrument that measures the DISPUTED quantity directly), and count the carrier's recovery-gated procs over the same window. Compare against sim lastBullet firings.

flags.estimate: alliesLowestHp count 1 — resolved to the leftmost ally (the documented stand-in).
flags.reasoning: '1 ally with the lowest HP percentage' is genuinely indeterminate at scope lock: the boss deals no damage, so every ally sits at 100% and the real game's selection never has a defined answer in this fight. The schema documents alliesLowestHp resolving to leftmost as a deliberate stand-in. Since only a recovery EVENT (not an amount) is emitted, WHICH ally receives it matters only if some ally has an on-recovery consumer — then the stand-in is load-bearing and could credit or starve the wrong unit.
flags.recipe: Only decidable on a damaging boss (out of v1 scope). At scope lock, bound the blast radius instead: A/B the comp with the target forced to each slot and check whether any teammate's on-recovery proc count moves. If it does, the stand-in is load-bearing and the comp needs a note.

flags.estimate: Inexpressible — empty effects array; 0 damage impact.
flags.reasoning: No StatKey covers incoming-healing amplification, and the engine models no HP amounts, so there is nothing for it to scale. I am flagging rather than silently dropping because a future heal-magnitude consumer (or an HP-scaling ATK conversion fed by healing) would make this line live. Note the trigger identity is still worth pinning: fullBurstEnter fires on ANY team Full Burst, so a wrong read here (burstCast) would under-fire in multi-caster comps.
flags.recipe: No measurement needed while the engine has no HP pool. Revisit if an HP-amount model lands; then the line needs a new StatKey (e.g. incomingHealingPct) rather than a re-tune.

flags.estimate: Ungated — condition always TRUE at scope lock.
flags.reasoning: The gate is trivially satisfied on a partless, non-damaging boss (mary can never drop below 50%). Modeling it ungated is faithful HERE, but it is an explicit scope-lock assumption, not a claim about the kit: on any boss that deals damage the DEF buff would have real downtime. Recording it so the assumption is visible if the sim ever gains a damage-taken model.
flags.recipe: Only testable on a damaging boss (out of v1 scope). If HP modeling lands, this needs a self-HP-threshold block gate primitive (none exists today).

flags.reasoning: The MAGNITUDE is not a ⛑ (it is verbatim in the kit text). The flag is on its INERTNESS: defPct is documented inert in v1, so this buff moves zero damage today. I am keeping it per HARD RULE 7 (retain the stat buff for a future consumer) and flagging so a later reader does not mistake 'present in the override' for 'affecting the board'.
flags.recipe: No measurement. Verify inertness cheaply by A/B toggling the block in the harness — expect a byte-identical total (that A/B IS the independent check; no footage needed).

flags.estimate: Mary contributes ZERO damage effects and ZERO offensive stat buffs. Her board footprint is her own SG normals plus whatever a teammate's recovery-trigger consumer produces.
flags.reasoning: Whole-picture check: all five kit lines are sustain (2 heals, 1 healing amp, 1 DEF buff, plus their activation clauses). This is a genuine, kit-faithful result — NOT a sign of an under-parsed kit — but it is exactly the profile that gets wrongly dismissed as 'skip, defensive'. Per the tandem/cross-unit HARD RULE the heals are retained precisely because they are the interface a partner damage kit reads. Also note she is a SUPPORTER (static ATK 98,367 at Base 5), so her own SG normals are modest.
flags.recipe: Run her in the harness alongside an on-recovery carrier and assert the carrier's recovery-gated proc count > 0 (S1 lastBullet + burst cast). A solo run asserting ~zero skill/burst-bucket damage is the complementary pin.
